title: Scheduling custodian: tiered warmup and eviction policy for continuous batching
creator: Lena Park
description: Problem: Continuous batching improves GPU utilization but makes cache residency and preemption more complex: warmup costs for KV caches, unpredictable GPU memory pressure, and unfair slowdowns for small-latency tenants. Proposal: introduce a lightweight 'scheduling custodian' subsystem that enforces tiered warmup / eviction windows and probabilistic preemption budgets to balance SLO targets across tenants while reducing KV thrash and unnecessary KV reloads. The custodian coordinates with the existing batcher and KV manager to make admission and interrupt decisions that consider: tenant SLO (p99 latency target), KV residency score, recent cold-start cost, and GPU slab pressure. This ticket scopes design, implementation plan, tests, and rollout for the custodian's first iteration.
acceptance_criteria: Custodian implements 3-tier warmup state machine (hot / warm / cold) per tenant and exposes residency_score metric
Preemption decisions use a configurable token budget constrained by tenant priority and observed p99 latency; default policy reduces preemptions for tenants with <10% KV miss-rate
End-to-end tests show >=15% reduction in extra KV fetches during bursty traffic compared to baseline under synthetic mixed workloads
No regression in <99th-percentile latency for top-tier SLO tenants during canary (compare against runtime-1.20 baseline)
Feature gate and telemetry added so rollout can be rolled back within one hour if GPU OOM or latency regressions exceed thresholds
design_notes: Tiered warmup: 'hot' (no preemption, KV pinned), 'warm' (soft reservations, allow preemption with backoff), 'cold' (evictable; warmup on next request incurs KV fetch)
Residency score: composite metric computed from KV touch recency, hit rate, and inferred warmup cost (estimated tokens fetched * avg fetch latency)
Preemption budgets: per-tenant token buckets replenished on successful low-latency windows; bursts consume budget and cause temporary deprioritization
Handoff window: when a tenant moves from one GPU to another (autoscaling, eviction), custodian records a short-lived 'handoff' tag to avoid double-eviction thrash for replicas
GPU slab hints: expose small integer hints from custodian to GPU allocator to prefer compacting cold slabs first during memory pressure
Compatibility: custodian API is a thin controller with clear contract to batcher (admit/reject/suspend/resume) and to kv-manager (pin/unpin/evict-by-score)
Observability: metrics needed - custodian_decisions{action,tenant}, residency_score, preemption_budget_level, kv_miss_deltas, gpu_slab_pressure
Configuration: default policy conservative; allow tenant overrides via weight and sla_tier. Admins can tune warmup windows and budget refill rates
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike): implement residency_score prototype in kv-manager and synth bench (2w)
Phase 2: custodian core service that subscribes to batcher and kv-manager events, exposes admit/suspend API, and records metrics (3w)
Phase 3: integrate probabilistic preemption budget and handoff tags; add GPU slab hint path (2w)
Phase 4: tests and stability hardening; add feature flag and rollout telemetry (1w)
Expected owners: Diego (engineer) + review from Marcus Klein (infra), Aisha Patel (SRE), and Priya Rao (ML infra)
test_plan: Unit: residency_score math, state transitions, budget refill logic
Integration: synthetic multi-tenant bench with mixed short/long sequences to measure KV fetchs and p99 latency
Chaos: simulate GPU OOM and abrupt node eviction to validate handoff window prevents thrash
Canary: enable on 5% of runtime fleet with telemetry-driven gating; compare p95/p99 and KV fetch deltas
Customer-sim: replay anonymized production traces (obfuscated) to validate policy under real workload shapes
rollout_plan: Canary 5% for 24h: monitor custodian_decisions, kv_miss_deltas, gpu_oom_rate, p99_lantency for SLO-tier tenants
If metrics stable, expand to 25% for 48h, then 100% over one week with progressive budget tightening
Fallback: revert flag or set global preemption_budget to zero to disable custodian preemption path
risks: Incorrect residency_score tuning could over-pin memory and trigger GPU OOMs; mitigation: conservative defaults and out-of-memory circuit-breaker
Budget-based preemption may unfairly punish bursty but latency-sensitive tenants; mitigation: SLO-tier overrides and telemetry-driven adjustments
Cross-service race (batcher / kv-manager / custodian) could create transient inconsistency; mitigation: idempotent commands and lightweight lease tokens for handoff
Increased control-plane CPU from custodian bookkeeping at scale; mitigation: sampling and aggregation heuristics
